title: Give a value a useful name
body: A variable is a name that points to a value. Python uses the equals sign to connect the name on the left with the value on the right.

title: A name can point to a new value
body: Python reads the current score, adds five, and then makes score point to the result.
takeaway: Reassignment replaces the value associated with the name.

title: Your turn: follow the value
explanation: coins begins at 4. The second line adds 3 and reassigns the result, so the printed value is 7.

wrong_feedback.a: That is the original value. Look at the reassignment on line two.
wrong_feedback.c: Python evaluates the expression before assigning it; it does not store the expression as text.

hint: Trace coins one line at a time: 4, then 4 + 3.

title: Values come in different shapes
body: Python uses types to decide what operations make sense. Integers are whole numbers, floats contain decimals, strings are text, and booleans are True or False.
code:
age = 24          # int
price = 4.50      # float
city = "Boston"  # str
ready = True      # bool
takeaway: The type belongs to the value, and Python can inspect it with type().

title: Convert text before doing math
body: Input often arrives as text. int() converts numeric text into a whole number that Python can add.

title: Your turn: spot the result type
body: In Python 3, the / operator always returns a float. What is printed?
explanation: Regular division uses / and returns a float, even when the mathematical answer is a whole number.

wrong_feedback.a: The value is four, but / represents it as a float: 4.0.
wrong_feedback.c: Both operands are numbers, so division is valid.

hint: Remember the lesson’s rule for the / operator.

title: Let your program make a decision
body: An if statement runs an indented block only when its condition is True. The colon begins the block and indentation shows what belongs inside it.
takeaway: Condition, colon, then an indented action.

title: Choose between two paths
body: else supplies the path Python follows when the if condition is False.
takeaway: Only one branch in this if/else pair will run.

title: Your turn: choose the branch
explanation: 82 is not greater than or equal to 90, so the if condition is False and the else branch runs.

wrong_feedback.c: An if/else pair selects one branch, not both.

hint: Evaluate 82 >= 90 before looking at either print statement.

title: Quick review: combine the ideas
body: Trace the variable, then evaluate the condition. What is printed?
code:
level = 2
level = level + 1
if level == 3:
    print("Unlocked")
explanation: level becomes 3, making level == 3 true. Python enters the indented block and prints Unlocked.

wrong_feedback.b: Trace the reassignment before evaluating the condition.
wrong_feedback.c: The assignment, condition, colon, and indentation are all valid Python.

hint: What value does level have after line two?
